correctness.rationale: The regular isotropic-coordinate extension of the subextremal Kerr t=0 slice is complete, vacuum and two-ended; its stationary axial shift has zero spatial divergence, hence tr K=0. The outer horizon sphere is a MOTS with A=4πS₂, S₂=2Mr₊, and J=aM. BCK eq. (22) is the exact outward-unit-normal stability operator at this spin. Its strictly positive simple principal eigenfunction, normalized by its integral, is fixed by rotations. The axisymmetric reduction therefore gives the full principal eigenvalue. The Legendre form comparison for the reduction gives λ₂≥2/S₂+min V; the smooth trial u=89+33z² belongs to the spherical operator domain. An independent integer-interval replay evaluated the exact BCK potential and checked monotonicity, enclosed the Rayleigh quotient by panel integration, and bounded the Temple variance using a fixed center (the variance at the true Rayleigh quotient can only be smaller). With outward integer rounding it proved λ₁>0.0826332 and λ₁A>2.3696992, while 8δ<1.220747, as well as the frozen area and deficit intervals. This verifies the stated counterexample, its quantitative headline bounds and stability without relying on the missing source script. The frozen Temple chain rounded the variance and then rounded the lower bound in the unsafe direction by about 8×10⁻⁸; the asserted result is nevertheless independently certified using tighter bounds. An analytic sign and margin check is also available: substituting f=√R into the exact operator gives Hf/f=c₀+c₁/R. For subextremal Kerr c₁≥0 and the minimum is c₀+c₁/S₂=(r₊²−a²)/S₂². Integrating Hf against the positive ground state gives λ₁A≥4π(r₊−M)/M, already larger than 8δ at this spin, though weaker than the headline numerical bound.
residual_risks: The frozen source script was not supplied and its stated printout and last digits for its intermediate values were not certified by that script in this audit. The independent replay checks the decisive comparisons with its own enclosures, rather than claiming provenance of the frozen digits.
The slow-rotation and near-extremal numerical trend is not used to conclude an optimal constant or a general rate.

value.rationale: The claim separates qualitative extremal rigidity from a particular quantitative spectral estimate in the exact Kerr family, where the relevant deficit, spin and stability normalization are fixed by geometry. A strict, well-separated counterexample to the stated coefficient in its admitted window is useful even at one point: it prevents using that coefficient in any general estimate of this form. The gap is not a rounding or convention artifact. This is not evidence against every linear vanishing law or for a particular exponent.
residual_risks: Optimal coefficient, exact extremal asymptotics and applicability to other initial data remain open in this review.
